correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the normalized B=1 proof for arbitrary holomorphic maps into the open half-strip. Its bounded Dirichlet majorant is the Brownian exit expectation: the exit ordinate has the prescribed mean and takes both signs with positive probability, giving a strictly positive gap inside. Bounded harmonic radial convergence applies to both the majorant pulled back to the disk and the imaginary part; no assumption on the boundary real part is needed. The Fourier coefficients of the limiting triangular datum are 2/lambda_j^2. The conformal inverse has a boundary extension away from the single preimage of infinity; bounded analytic uniqueness rules out a positive-measure preimage of that point. Thus inner maps give equality, whereas non-inner maps give a positive integrated gap on a positive-measure set. Composing with an automorphism (and optionally a disk power) realizes any center. For the corner law the derivative is (2/pi) log|coth(pi(X+iY)/4)|; z coth z=1+O(|z|^2) gives the requisite uniform derivative error, whose integral from 0 to X is O(X(X^2+Y^2)). Rechecking the repair confirms both the limit from the prior calculation and the claims it retains.

The boundary data converge uniformly as p decreases to 1; at p=1 the coefficients are 2/lambda_j^2. Passing to the limit at any X>0 yields the very profile in the frozen Finding. Conformal boundary realization then provides the sharp bound. This does not rely on the divergent A_p.

value.rationale: The complete extremizer test distinguishes all equality maps, including nonunivalent maps, rather than merely constructing a conformal witness. The joint estimate pinpoints why the initial response changes from finite linear slope at a fixed off-center ordinate to the centered logarithmic singularity. Its uniform error covers paths for which separate one-variable expansions would not determine the crossover. These are independently useful statements about equality and asymptotic scale in a natural sharp bound already implied by prior work.
